title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_1RA0RE_1RD1LA_---0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_1RA0RE_1RD1LA_---0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a Collatz-like map g → 3g/2 + c on a counter, whose residues mod 4 drive a slowly growing stack R; the inner sweep is proved in Lean, the epoch map is checked against simulation, and 300 epochs of it (about 10110 steps) show no halt. Like Antihydra, a proof would need control of the residues of a 3/2 map.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,556 cells have been visited and 46,581 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.52). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: The tape is a list of runs of 1s and gaps of 0s. At 109 steps (runs of 1s, with 0^k for k+1 zeros in a row): 44842 1688 0^2 4 0^848 11 0^7 4 0^15 4 0^17 4 0^19 4 0^11 4 0^17 8 0^27 4 0 4; the end 4 0^11 4 0^17 8 0^27 4 0 4 has been the same since 107 steps, and the long runs and gaps at the left end change between visits.

claims.title: One sweep, and many sweeps
claims.text: X(n,m) = 0^inf A> 0 1^n 000 1111 0^m R: one sweep takes X(2k+2, m+4) to X(2k+8, m) in 6k+50 steps, for every k and every tape R; iterated, X(2k+2, 4j) R reaches X(2k+2+6j) R in j(6k+50)+9j(j-1) steps.

claims.title: The epoch map
claims.text: From E(g,R) = 0^inf A> 0 1 0^g R the next epoch is E(3g/2 + c, R'), where c (one of -9, -6, -3, +6) and R' depend only on g mod 4 and R. Checked for four values of g in each class for every R tried, and against direct simulation epoch by epoch up to 3·1011 steps.

claims.title: 300 epochs without a halt
claims.text: Iterating the epoch map with g an exact integer from g = 4206: 300 epochs, g up to about 10<sup>55</sup> (about 10<sup>110</sup> steps), no halt; the right part R grows from 13 to about 190 runs. This rests on the epoch map being independent of g within a class, which is checked, not proved.

claims.title: Why a halt looks unlikely
claims.text: Each epoch rewrites only the first few runs of R, like the top of a stack, and R grows by about 0.6 runs per epoch, with the real residues and with random ones alike. Every halting R found in a random search contains a lone 1, which the run never makes near the front; a halt would need the front to dig down through a stack that keeps getting deeper.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The epoch map g → 3g/2 + c is Collatz-like; next steps: prove the class map in Lean for the R that occur, and describe R exactly as a stack automaton.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 47,556 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The exact epoch map, iterated to about 10<sup>110</sup> steps: no halt.

sections.heading: A counter that grows by half each time, and a stack it writes into
html: Watch the left end of the tape. Every so often it looks like this: the head in state A just left of the tape, a single 1, a long gap of g zeros, and then a short, slowly changing part R:
These moments are the epochs. The gap sizes are 18, 24, 30, 42, 60, 84, 120, 174, 258, 378, 564, 840, 1254, 1878, ...: each about one and a half times the last.

<svg viewBox='0 0 560 120' role='img' aria-label='one sweep: the block of ones grows by 6, the marker moves 4 to the right' style='width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:12px var(--mono)'><rect x='10' y='20' width='150' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='85' y='35' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>1^n</text><rect x='190' y='20' width='28' height='22' fill='var(--head)'/><text x='204' y='58' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>1111</text><rect x='218' y='20' width='300' height='22' fill='none' stroke='var(--line-strong)'/><text x='368' y='35' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>gap 0^m</text><rect x='10' y='76' width='186' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='103' y='91' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>1^(n+6)</text><rect x='222' y='76' width='28' height='22' fill='var(--head)'/><rect x='250' y='76' width='268' height='22' fill='none' stroke='var(--line-strong)'/><text x='384' y='91' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>gap 0^(m-4)</text></svg>

Inside an epoch the machine sweeps back and forth. Each sweep adds 6 ones to a block at the left and pushes a marker 1111 4 cells further into the gap (this rule is proved in Lean for every n). When the marker reaches R, the block has grown to about 3g/2 cells; the machine rewrites the front of R and turns the block into the next gap. So

a Collatz-like map, the same kind as the famous Antihydra's. Which c, and how R changes, depends only on g mod 4 and on R. The residues of g are pseudo-random, and they are written one per epoch into R, which acts like a stack: only its top few runs change each time.

Can it halt?

The machine halts only when, in state A, it reads a 1 followed by a 0 in a particular place. Every halting R found by search contains a lone 1, which the run does not produce. A halt needs the front of R to dig deep, but R keeps growing (about 0.6 runs per epoch). Iterating the exact map 300 epochs (to about 10110 steps) shows no halt. Nobody can yet prove that it never happens, for the same reason as for Antihydra: we cannot control the residues of a 3/2 map.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.52). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,556 cells (37,924 left of the start, 23 right), with a density of 1s of 0.979.

summary: A Collatz-like 3/2 map g -> 3g/2 + c on a gap of zeros at the left end, whose residues mod 4 are written into a slowly growing stack on the right; the sweep rule is proved in Lean, the epoch map is checked; open.
